summary: This document defines the data types and management policy for the IPFIX information model. The model is maintained as the IANA IPFIX Information Elements registry, with initial contents from RFC 5102. The IPFIX protocol uses it to encode measured traffic and related information.

eli5.summary: This is the dictionary of every kind of fact about network traffic that can be reported, and what each fact means.

questions: what is an ipfix information element
what data types does ipfix define
how are ipfix information elements registered
what does the post prefix mean in ipfix
subtitle: The shared vocabulary of data types and naming rules that describes every fact an IPFIX flow report can carry.

tldr.problem: The IPFIX protocol says how to transmit flow information, but it does not say which Information Elements (source address, packet count, sampling rate and so on) can be sent or what types they have.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7012 defines the properties every Information Element must have, a fixed set of abstract data types and semantics, naming rules, and the process for extending the model through an IANA registry.
tldr.outcome: The IANA registry, not this document, is now the normative list of Information Elements. RFC 7012 obsoletes RFC 5102 and moves the element definitions out of the RFC.

today: RFC 7012 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 5102, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it. The IANA "IPFIX Information Elements" registry is the normative reference for the elements themselves.

sections.title: Why an Information Model Is Needed
sections.content:
The IPFIX protocol (RFC 7011) defines how Information Elements are transmitted and how a set of basic data types is encoded. What it does not list is which Information Elements exist. Examples are flow attributes such as the source IP address or the number of packets, and facts about the Metering Process and Exporting Process such as the Observation Point, the sampling rate or the Flow timeout interval.

RFC 7012 fills that gap by giving an overview of the IPFIX information model and specifying its data types. The complete list lives in the IANA "IPFIX Information Elements" registry, whose initial values came from RFC 5102.

The RFC admits that "information model" is used loosely. The model does not specify relationships between Information Elements or a concrete encoding, and other encodings, for example XML-based ones, can be applied besides the one used by the IPFIX protocol.
sections.eli5: A traffic report needs a list of the kinds of facts it can contain. This document explains how that list is built and kept in order.

sections.title: What Every Information Element Must Define
sections.content:
Every Information Element must have a name, a numeric elementId, a description, a dataType and a status. The status is either current or deprecated, and all newly defined elements are current. A description of a string or octetArray element that has length constraints must state them.

Enterprise-specific elements must also carry an enterpriseId. An enterprise may define elements without registering them with IANA, but when they are used outside the enterprise, the identifier must be made globally unique by combining it with an enterprise number from the IANA private enterprise registry.

Optional properties are dataTypeSemantics, units, range and reference. If a range is given, values outside it are invalid and must not be exported. Two further properties support registry maintenance: revision, which starts at 0 and goes up by one for each revision, and date of the entry of that revision into the registry.

By default an element has a scope given in its definition. In Data Records defined by Options Templates, the scope can be narrowed further with one or more scope fields.
sections.eli5: Each fact in the dictionary needs a name, a number, a description and a type, like a label on a jar. Some jars also say what unit they use.

sections.title: Naming Conventions and the post Prefix
sections.content:
Names should be descriptive and must be unique within the registry. They must start with a lowercase letter, and composed names capitalise the first letter of each component except the first, for example sourceMacAddress and destinationIPv4Address. Acronyms are lowercase except those that mix cases, such as IPv4 and IPv6. Enterprise-specific elements should be prefixed with a vendor name.

The prefix post has a special meaning. A middlebox may change flow properties such as the DSCP value or the source IP address. If the Observation Point sits before such a middlebox, the element ipClassOfService reports the value as seen there, while postIpClassOfService reports the changed value. A post element need not be observed at the Observation Point; it may be obtained within the Observation Domain by other means considered sufficiently reliable, such as analysing the marker's marking tables.
sections.eli5: Names follow one spelling pattern, like camelCase, so they are easy to guess. A name starting with post means the value after something in the middle changed it.

sections.title: The Type Space
sections.content:
Data types are abstract, independent of encoding; the IPFIX encodings are in RFC 7011. The integral types are unsigned8, unsigned16, unsigned32, unsigned64, signed8, signed16, signed32 and signed64. The others are float32, float64, boolean, macAddress, octetArray, string, ipv4Address and ipv6Address, four time types with second, millisecond, microsecond and nanosecond precision, and three structured types: basicList, subTemplateList and subTemplateMultiList, which are defined with RFC 6313.

Integral types can be qualified by a data type semantic, which applies only to numeric types. quantity is the default and is a measured value. totalCounter and deltaCounter are unsigned counters that wrap to zero at the type's limit; a total counter counts independently of export, while a delta counter is reset to 0 each time it is exported or expires without export. identifier values can only be compared for equality, and flags are bit fields that must be of an unsigned type.

New abstract data types and semantics require Standards Action and must be defined in IETF Standards Track documents updating this one.
sections.eli5: Every fact has a type, like whole number, text or yes/no. A counter is like a bike odometer, and a delta counter is like a trip meter that resets each time you look at it.

sections.title: Identifiers and Categories
sections.content:
Identifiers for registry elements are assigned by IANA in the range 1 to 32767. The sub-range 1 to 127 is compatible with the field types of NetFlow version 9 (RFC 3954) for historical reasons, and IANA assigns new elements the lowest available identifier in 128 to 32767. Enterprise-specific identifiers use the same range, and identifier 0 is also reserved for them, and are made distinct by the accompanying enterprise identifier.

RFC 7012 no longer lists the elements. Section 5 only keeps a historical note: RFC 5102 grouped them into 12 categories, from identifiers, header fields and timestamps to counters and padding. These categories were not carried into the registry.

For elements derived from packet fields or Packet Treatment whose value may change within a Flow, the exported value is by default determined by the first packet observed, unless the description says otherwise.
sections.eli5: Each fact gets a number, like a locker number. Companies can invent their own facts, and they add their company number so lockers never clash.

sections.title: Extending the Model Through IANA
sections.content:
New Information Element definitions are added to the IANA registry through Expert Review, using the process in RFC 7013. The experts are called IE-DOCTORS and are appointed by the IESG. Identifiers 1 to 127 may only be assigned to elements compatible with NetFlow version 9, as judged by one of the experts designated as a NetFlow version 9 expert. A revision or deprecation of an element that was defined by an RFC requires IETF consensus.

The document also records what IANA did. It added Revision and Date columns, set existing revisions to 0, renamed reserved elements with identifiers 127 or less to "Assigned for NetFlow v9 compatibility", and added a note that references to RFC 5102 stay as historical record. IANA also created a subregistry for MPLS label types, filled from element #46, mplsTopLabelType, which has five initial types, and deprecated the old XML schema urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:ipfix-info.

The RFC says use of XML is not mandatory for IPFIX deployment, and that Collectors should not poll the IANA registry directly at runtime.
sections.eli5: New facts can be added to the dictionary only after a small group of experts checks them. That keeps the dictionary tidy.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The information model does not by itself introduce security issues, but the attributes it defines may be sensitive for privacy or business reasons. For example, exporting header field values may make attacks possible for the receiver of the data that would otherwise be possible only for direct observers of the flows on the data path.

For that reason the protocol that carries the information must provide integrity and confidentiality. Those procedures are defined in the IPFIX protocol document, RFC 7011.
sections.eli5: A traffic report can reveal private things, so the way it is sent must keep it safe from tampering and prying eyes.
